label: EdgePoint R8
description: EdgePoint R8 (EP-R8) - 8x 1G RJ45 data ports (6 plain + 2 RJ45/SFP combination) plus 2x 1G SFP cages. eth1-eth2 source 54V or 24V passive PoE at 1.4A 4-pair; eth3-eth7 source 24V/0.7A 2-pair passive PoE. eth0 accepts 54V/1.5A passive PoE in; a separate RJ45 PoE In port is power-only and carries no data. 40 W max excluding PoE output; 284 W PoE envelope on the 54 V / 6 A DC input. Passive PoE only - no 802.3af/at negotiation on any port.

poe.note: DERIVED ENVELOPE, not a quoted budget - Ubiquiti prints no "PoE budget" row for this box on either surface. The two figures it does print give the headroom exactly: "Power method (1) DC terminal block, (2) RJ45 (PoE In and eth0), 54V DC, 6A input" = 324 W, and "Max. power consumption 40W (Excludes PoE output)", so at most 324 - 40 = 284 W can leave the seven PSE ports on the stated DC-input configuration. Same arithmetic shape as devices/ubiquiti/ep-s16.json, devices/ubiquiti/uisp-r.json and devices/ubiquiti/er-6p.json. A box fed instead by its two 54V/1.5A passive PoE inputs has 2 x 81 = 162 W of input and therefore at most 162 - 40 = 122 W for its own PSE ports; a lab that powers it that way states its own figure. Read 2026-11-19: https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgePoint_DS.pdf (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 6,571,516 B, 12 pp; page 7 "Hardware Specifications EP-R8") and https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/ep-r8 (HTTP 200, 578,035 B, rendered spec table - not the 609,911 B front page). NOT an 802.3 standard anywhere: every output row is 4-pair or 2-pair PASSIVE PoE with no detection, so a 48 V 802.3af/at PD will not negotiate; "PoE In" is DC only with no data.

notes:
Census, all from the vendor datasheet text layer (https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgePoint_DS.pdf - 200, application/pdf, 6,571,516 B, 12 pp, "Models: EP-R6, EP-R8, EP-S16", page 7 = EP-R8 table, read 2026-11-19) unless stated; the rendered techspecs table at https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/ep-r8 prints the same rows.

PORTS - page 7: "Serial Console Port (1) RJ45 Serial Port"; "Data Ports (6) 10/100/1000 RJ45 Ports, (2) 10/100/1000 RJ45/SFP Combination Ports". Eight copper positions (eth0-eth7) plus two 1G SFP cages; the console is a line, not a link (research/console-is-a-line-not-an-interface.md). The separate "PoE In Port (1) RJ45 Port" is a power inlet, not an interface: "PoE In is DC Only, No Data".

which copper positions are the two combination ones is NOT published - the datasheet gives the count ("(2) 10/100/1000 RJ45/SFP Combination Ports") and the PoE rows name eth0-eth7, but nothing pairs a copper position with sfp1 or sfp2. The pairing is left undeclared rather than guessed: an empty field is a question, a guessed comboWith is a bug that shows up when a lab cables ten links into eight positions. A source for the pairing (panel artwork with readable labels, or the EdgeOS default config) would let it be declared.

PoE OUTPUT - page 7: "Passive PoE Output (2) 54V or 24V / 1.4A, 4-Pair (+1, 2, 4, 5; -3, 6, 7, 8) Passive PoE, eth1 to eth2" and "(5) 24V / 0.7A, 2-Pair (+4, 5; -7, 8) Passive PoE, eth3 to eth7". So eth1-eth2 carry 75.6 W at 54 V (33.6 W at 24 V) and eth3-eth7 carry 16.8 W each, all passive. Seven PSE ports in total.

PoE INPUT - page 7: "Passive PoE Input (2) 54V / 1.5A, 4-Pair ... Passive PoE, eth0 and PoE In". eth0 therefore declares `poeIn: 40` - the vendor's own "Max. power consumption 40W (Excludes PoE output)" is what the box draws from a PoE source; the 1.5 A row is the port's input capacity, not a draw, and is not used as one.

WHAT WAS WRONG - the row had the two PoE facts inverted and no budget. It declared `poeOut` on eth0 and eth1 with class "PoE" (802.3af, 48 V negotiated) on a box that has no 802.3 detection at all, and it declared no PoE on eth2-eth7, so five real PSE ports were dry. eth0, which the vendor lists under PoE INPUT and not under PoE OUTPUT, was modelled as a power source; `poe-pd` was missing. With no `poe` block, `engine/simulator.js` opened `computePoe()` with `if (!dev.poeBudget) continue;` and skipped the box, so the two ports that did claim PoE could power nothing and `show power inline` reported a budget of zero.

NOT MODELLED - no 802.3af, 802.3at or 802.3bt capability: the datasheet prints no 802.3 row for this chassis, only the passive rows above. No PoE++ and no SFP+ rate: the cages are "10/100/1000 ... Combination", i.e. 1G.
